title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Declaration Lead Times, Late Cut-offs, Review Standard and Approval Validity
content:
Four time parameters of Dangerous Goods Acceptance vary by category: how many calendar days ahead of the scheduled departure (ETD) a signed declaration counts as on time, how many hours ahead of the cargo cut-off a late declaration can still be taken, the service standard in hours within which the line decides a review, and for how many calendar days an approval covers loading once granted.

| Category | On-time declaration: calendar days before ETD | Late declaration still taken: hours before cargo cut-off | Review decided within (hours) | Approval covers loading for (calendar days after approval) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AHL DG Limited Quantity | 3 | 48 | 24 | 30 |
| AHL DG Class 9 Standard | 5 | 48 | 24 | 21 |
| AHL DG Flammables and Corrosives | 7 | 72 | 48 | 21 |
| AHL DG Toxics and Oxidizers | 7 | 72 | 48 | 14 |
| AHL DG Compressed Gases | 10 | 96 | 72 | 14 |
| AHL DG Special Approval | 21 | 168 | 120 | 10 |

## Units at a glance

- The lead time and the approval period are counted in calendar days.
- The late cut-off is counted in hours back from the cargo cut-off of the sailing.
- The review figure is a service standard for the line, expressed in hours.

## Comparisons

Moving up the ranks, the notice demanded and the late cut-off never shrink and the approval period never grows, with AHL DG Special Approval at both extremes (21 days of notice, 168 hours of late cut-off, 10 days of validity). AHL DG Flammables and Corrosives and AHL DG Toxics and Oxidizers share their notice, cut-off and review figures and differ only in approval validity.
